Install omarchy-nvim on Omarchy

Omarchy Neovim packages LazyVim, a popular configuration framework for the Neovim text editor, with its plugins pre-built and cached so you're not waiting on downloads and compilation the first time you open it. LazyVim turns plain Neovim into a full IDE-like environment: sensible default keybindings, file navigation, LSP support, and a large pre-configured plugin set, while still letting you customize anything. It's a terminal-based editor experience, not a separate graphical application.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add omarchy-nvim
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 2026.8.13-1:
    pacman -Qi omarchy-nvim

Open and use omarchy-nvim

omarchy-nvim has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql omarchy-nvim | grep /usr/bin/

omarchy-nvim requirements and compatibility

  • Neovim 0.11.2+ (built with LuaJIT)
  • Git 2.19.0+
  • A C compiler (for nvim-treesitter)
  • A Nerd Font recommended for icons

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • neovim
  • git

Free and open source (MIT licensed). License: MIT.

Frequently asked questions

How do I install omarchy-nvim on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add omarchy-nvim. The download is 36.5 MB and it takes 65.4 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is omarchy-nvim free?

Free and open source (MIT licensed). The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall omarchy-nvim?

Run omarchy pkg drop omarchy-nvim. It removes the package from your system.

What does omarchy-nvim depend on?

The package declares 2 dependencies: neovim, git. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is omarchy-nvim a desktop app?

No. omarchy-nvim has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is omarchy-nvim in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as omarchy-nvim (version 2026.8.13-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. LazyVim makes it. Project site: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim. This site is unofficial and not affiliated with Omarchy or Omacom.
